sentences.en: Hello everybody, I'm Gemma Spake and welcome back to The Psychology of Your 20s, the podcast where we talk through the biggest changes, moments, and transitions of our 20s
sentences.zh: 大家好，我是杰玛·斯派克，欢迎回到《你二十岁的心理学》，这是一档我们一起探讨二十岁时的巨大变化、重要时刻与人生过渡的播客，

sentences.en: and what they mean for our psychology.
sentences.zh: 以及这些变化对我们心理的意义。

sentences.en: Hello everybody, welcome back to the show, welcome back to the podcaSt.
sentences.zh: 大家好，欢迎回到节目，欢迎回到播客。

sentences.en: It is so great to have you here back for another episode today.
sentences.zh: 很高兴今天大家能来收听新的一期节目。

sentences.en: We welcome back one of our favorite, my favorite guests.
sentences.zh: 今天我们迎来了我们最喜爱的、我最喜爱的嘉宾之一。

sentences.en: She has been on the show so many times.
sentences.zh: 她已经无数次来到我们的节目了。

sentences.en: She is one of the global experts on attachment style, relationships, how to find healthy love.
sentences.zh: 她是依恋类型、亲密关系以及如何找到健康爱情领域的全球专家之一。

sentences.en: She's written two books.
sentences.zh: 她写过两本书。

sentences.en: She has coached thousands of people and has done more research on this than probably any other person.
sentences.zh: 她指导过成千上万的人，在这方面的研究可能比任何其他人都多。

sentences.en: The other day, I got an email from her about this new theory that she's been working on.
sentences.zh: 前几天，我收到她的一封邮件，谈到她一直在研究的一个新理论。

sentences.en: It's called The Six Stages of a Relationship and I just knew we had to talk about it because it is incredibly accurate.
sentences.zh: 它被称为“关系的六个阶段”，我当时就知道我们必须聊聊这个，因为它简直准得不可思议。

sentences.en: First of all, it is so accurate how it represents almost every relationship we find ourselves in.
sentences.zh: 首先，它如何精准地映射出我们身处其中的几乎每一段关系，这太准了。

sentences.en: And I also think that learning about these six stages, especially in our 20s, what they represent, what they mean, could help us all be more realistic about love
sentences.zh: 而且我也认为，了解这六个阶段，尤其是在我们二十岁的时候，它们代表什么、意味着什么，可以帮助我们所有人对爱情保持更多现实的期待，

sentences.en: and also understand the highs and lows of dating and the highs and lows of devotion and being with somebody long-term.
sentences.zh: 并且理解约会的高潮与低谷，以及长相厮守和长期伴侣关系的高潮与低谷。

sentences.en: Without further ado, here she is.
sentences.zh: 废话不多说，她来了。

sentences.en: Tyese Gibson, welcome to the psychology of your 20s again.
sentences.zh: 泰丝·吉布森，欢迎再次来到《你二十岁的心理学》。

sentences.en: Thank you for having me.
sentences.zh: 谢谢邀请我来。

sentences.en: You're one of my favorite people to chat with and join podcasts with and just honestly catch up with.
sentences.zh: 你是我最喜欢聊天、一起做播客，老实说就是叙旧的人之一。

sentences.en: So it's really nice to be here.
sentences.zh: 所以能来到这里真的很高兴。

sentences.en: No, it's so lovely every time you come on the show and you've been on a couple of times.
sentences.zh: 不，每次你来节目都太棒了，而且你已经来过好几次了。

sentences.en: You're like my go-to attachment style expert.
sentences.zh: 你就像是我首选的依恋类型专家。

sentences.en: I love your in-depth knowledge.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢你深入的知识储备。

sentences.en: I love how you talk about these topics.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢你谈论这些话题的方式。

sentences.en: I've kind of spoiled my next question, which is tell the listeners a little bit about yourself and what kind of work you do.
sentences.zh: 我刚刚其实有点剧透了我的下一个问题，那就是请向听众简单介绍一下你自己以及你从事怎样的工作。

sentences.en: Yeah, so to your point, I definitely work in the relationship space.
sentences.zh: 好的，正如你所说，我确实在亲密关系领域工作。

sentences.en: By trade, I am a counselor and coach and I've been in this space for quite a while now, more than a decade.
sentences.zh: 我的职业是一名咨询师和教练，在这个领域已经有一段时间了，超过了十年。

sentences.en: Um, and I tend to focus a lot in the attachment style space and I think that comes from, um, growing up with a fearful avoidant attachment style myself
sentences.zh: 嗯，我往往把很大一部分精力集中在依恋类型领域，我想这源于我自己成长过程中也有着恐惧型回避依恋风格，

sentences.en: and really pouring into trying to understand how to heal.
sentences.zh: 并真正全身心投入到试图理解如何疗愈的过程中。

sentences.en: Um, and I put a huge emphasis and focus not just on like understanding things and intellectualizing things, but actually rewiring because the more we can really
sentences.zh: 嗯，我非常强调和关注的不仅仅是理解事物和将其理性化，而是真正的重塑，因为我们越能真正地

sentences.en: dig into the subconscious and rewire our patterns and leverage neuroplasticity, that's where you get to see the real healing and change and growth.
sentences.zh: 深入潜意识、重塑我们的模式并利用神经可塑性，你就能看到真正的疗愈、改变和成长。

sentences.en: And so that was something that helped me on my journey so much and something that I'm always really excited to talk about and share with other people.
sentences.zh: 所以这对我的旅程帮助巨大，这也是我一直非常兴奋能与他人交流和分享的事情。

sentences.en: And you do like, just the way you talk about it is incredible.
sentences.zh: 而且你真的……你谈论它的方式太棒了。

sentences.en: And if you haven't listened to our other episodes, I think we did one on anxious attachment and avoidant.
sentences.zh: 如果你还没听过我们的其他节目，我想我们做过一期关于焦虑型依恋和回避型的节目。

sentences.en: Very much recommend going and listening to those.
sentences.zh: 非常推荐大家去听听。

sentences.en: Two of my favorite episodes that we've ever done, to be honeSt.
sentences.zh: 说实话，那是我做过的最喜欢的两期节目。

sentences.en: But today we're going to talk about
sentences.zh: 但今天我们要谈论的是

sentences.en: this, I guess, new theory that you've come up with, this new concept that you told me about and I was like, how come no one has ever shared this or talked about this
sentences.zh: 这个我猜是你新想出来的理论，这个你告诉我时我惊叹为什么以前从来没有人分享过或谈论过

sentences.en: or come up with this before?
sentences.zh: 或者以前从没有人提出过的新概念？

sentences.en: It is the six stage theory of relationships.
sentences.zh: 这就是关系的六阶段理论。

sentences.en: You know, I adore a theory.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我对各种理论爱不释手。

sentences.en: I adore like any kind of succinct explanation of like human phenomena.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢任何对人类现象的简明解释。

sentences.en: Can you just like quickly explain this one for me before we go into each stage
sentences.zh: 在我们逐一深入探讨每个阶段之前，你能否简单快速地

sentences.en: individually?
sentences.zh: 解释一下这个理论？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 可以的。

sentences.en: So the theory is essentially that every relationship has six stages.
sentences.zh: 所以这个理论的核心在于，每段关系都有六个阶段。

sentences.en: And I saw this through working with tens of thousands of clients that there's essentially a life cycle of every relationship.
sentences.zh: 我在与数万名客户共事的过程中看到了这一点，每段关系基本上都有一个生命周期。

sentences.en: And it starts at a high level.
sentences.zh: 它始于一个宏观层面。

sentences.en: We'll talk about them in detail for sure.
sentences.zh: 我们稍后肯定会详细讨论它们。

sentences.en: But at a high level, the first stage is the dating stage.
sentences.zh: 但从宏观来看，第一阶段是约会阶段。

sentences.en: And the intention of this stage is to really vet and get to know somebody and like see if they're a good fit for you and vice versa.
sentences.zh: 这个阶段的意图是真正去考核和了解某个人，看看他们是否适合你，反之亦然。

sentences.en: And then when we make a commitment, we move into the honeymoon stage.
sentences.zh: 然后当我们做出承诺时，我们就进入了蜜月阶段。

sentences.en: And this is the stage where essentially we have our rose-colored glasses on and we're all excited and everything feels great and it's easy and it's flowing.
sentences.zh: 在这个阶段，我们基本上戴着玫瑰色的眼镜，我们都很兴奋，一切感觉都棒极了，轻松且顺畅。

sentences.en: But we're usually showing ourselves still with a good bit of conditions.
sentences.zh: 但我们通常还是带着很多条件在展示自己。

sentences.en: We're on our best behavior.
sentences.zh: 我们表现得最好。

sentences.en: We're still people-pleasing maybe a little bit more than we otherwise would.
sentences.zh: 我们取悦他人的程度可能比平时还要稍微多一点。

sentences.en: We're not as comfortable.
sentences.zh: 我们还没那么自在。

sentences.en: And then we let down the mask and get comfortable.
sentences.zh: 然后我们摘下面具，开始感到自在。

sentences.en: And that actually is what draws us into the power struggle stage.
sentences.zh: 而这实际上正是把我们拉入权力之争阶段的原因。

sentences.en: And the power struggle stage you'll see is where statistically most people break up.
sentences.zh: 你会发现，权力之争阶段是统计学上大多数人分手的时候。

sentences.en: But the crazy part is that if you don't realize that in the long grand scheme of an entire relationship, like if you're going to marry somebody
sentences.zh: 但疯狂的是，如果你没有意识到在整段关系的宏大蓝图里——比如你要和某人结婚

sentences.en: and be with them for decades perhaps, the dating honeymoon power struggle are such a small snapshot of a whole relationship.
sentences.zh: 并和他们在一起几十年——约会、蜜月和权力之争只是整段关系中很小的一个剪影。

sentences.en: And if we don't ever have a relationship that makes beyond the power struggle, then people think that the whole relationship is like this high of infatuation, this low of fighting
sentences.zh: 如果我们从来没有经历过超越权力之争的关系，那么人们就会以为整段关系都是这样的：狂热的高潮，争吵的低谷

sentences.en: and more arguing and it breaks up.
sentences.zh: 以及更多的争吵，然后以分手告终。

sentences.en: And the reality is that the power struggle stage is actually something that presents this really unique and powerful opportunity to know each other more deeply,
sentences.zh: 而现实是，权力之争阶段实际上呈现了一个非常独特且强大的契机，让我们能更深入地了解彼此，

sentences.en: to work through conflict, to learn to hash things out, to learn each other and to get into a rhythm.
sentences.zh: 解决冲突，学会把事情摊开谈，了解彼此并进入一种默契的节奏。

sentences.en: And if we do that, we then progress into future stages which become the rhythm stage, the devotion stage, and eventually the everlasting stage which is where we have this true
sentences.zh: 如果我们做到了这一点，我们就会进入未来的阶段，也就是节奏阶段、奉献阶段，最后是永恒阶段，我们在那里对关系拥有了真实

sentences.en: and deep sense of lasting contentment in the relationship.
sentences.zh: 而深沉的持久满足感。

sentences.en: And so we'll boil into all of the stages of course in a lot of detail, but the theory essentially is rooted in the fact that every relationship, point blank period,
sentences.zh: 所以我们当然会非常详细地探讨所有阶段，但这个理论的根基基本上在于：毫无疑问，每一段关系

sentences.en: goes through this life cycle and there are specific rites of passage that we need to move from one stage to the next.
sentences.zh: 都要经历这个生命周期，而且我们需要通过特定的转折点才能从一个阶段走到下一个阶段。

sentences.en: So in order to continuously progress, there's actually things we have to learn and get good at with each other.
sentences.zh: 因此，为了持续取得进展，实际上有些事情我们必须共同学习并变得擅长。

sentences.en: And if we don't learn those rites of passage, we'll actually get stuck in a certain stage.
sentences.zh: 如果我们没有学会这些转折点，我们实际上就会被困在某个特定的阶段。

sentences.en: And the longer we're stuck in a stage without progressing, the more likely the relationship is to end.
sentences.zh: 我们在一个阶段困得越久而没有取得进展，关系走向结束的可能性就越大。

sentences.en: So what I find to be really meaningful is if people are struggling in relationships and they never really, you know, have a lasting relationship.
sentences.zh: 所以我发现真正有意义的是，如果人们在亲密关系中挣扎，却从来没有真正地（你知道的）拥有一段持久的关系。

sentences.en: It's always a year or two years, they break up, you know, things like this.
sentences.zh: 总是维持一年或两年，然后就分手了，诸如此类。

sentences.en: And they're looking for something longer lasting and more prominent for them.
sentences.zh: 而他们正在寻找对他们而言更持久、更显著的东西。

sentences.en: Or if somebody is in a stage now listening perhaps and they're like, I feel like I'm stuck in one of these stages and everything's rocky and we're not progressing.
sentences.zh: 或者如果有人现在正在收听，正处于某个阶段，心想：“我觉得我被困在这些阶段之一了，一切都摇摇欲坠，我们毫无进展。”

sentences.en: It's much less of the time that you have the wrong partner and much more of the time that you instead have the wrong tools and the wrong behaviors and relationships
sentences.zh: 很多时候并不是因为你找错了伴侣，更多时候是因为你用了错误的方法和错误的行为在处理关系，

sentences.en: that are actually keeping you stuck and not allowing you to progress.
sentences.zh: 这些其实让你停滞不前，不允许你取得进展。

sentences.en: And I would make a really strong argument having seen this firsthand that so often people are like, oh, maybe I'm not compatible with somebody.
sentences.zh: 根据我亲眼所见的经验，我可以非常有说服力地指出，人们经常会说：“哦，也许我和某人并不合适。”

sentences.en: Oh my gosh, what if it doesn't work out and they feel stuck?
